title: Sensex gains 512 points as banks and FMCG lead; rupee recovers to 93.92 a dollar
dek: Foreign buying and easing oil prices lifted the main indices on Monday, but mid-cap and small-cap shares fell, and domestic funds stayed net sellers.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
India's main stock indices rose on Monday, led by bank and consumer-goods shares, as foreign investors kept buying and crude oil prices eased. The BSE Sensex closed 512.34 points, or 0.63%, higher at 82,104.79, and the NSE Nifty 50 gained 146.80 points, or 0.58%, to end at 25,291.10, according to reports. One report put the Sensex close slightly lower, at 82,102.85.

The rupee strengthened by 27 paise to close at 93.92 against the US dollar, ending a two-day fall, after opening at 94.22 in the interbank foreign exchange market, reports said. It had closed at 94.19 on Friday. A stronger rupee makes imports, including crude oil, cheaper in rupee terms; reports attributed Monday's gain to foreign inflows into Indian shares and lower oil prices.

## What moved

The gains were narrow. The Nifty MidCap 100 index fell 0.51% and the Nifty SmallCap 100 lost 1.10%, according to reports, so more shares fell than rose in the broader market even as the headline indices climbed.

Among Sensex companies, State Bank of India, Eternal, Titan, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Bharti Airtel and Asian Paints were among the main gainers, while NTPC, InterGlobe Aviation, Tata Steel and Power Grid were among the laggards. Tata Consumer Products, Max Healthcare and ITC were among the top gainers in the Nifty. The Nifty FMCG and Nifty Bank indices rose the most among sectors, while pharmaceutical, automobile, metal and real estate shares fell, reports said.

Foreign institutional investors bought shares worth a net Rs 5,736 crore on Friday, while domestic institutional investors sold a net Rs 2,253 crore, their eleventh consecutive session of net selling, according to provisional figures cited in reports.

V K Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Investments, said "continuous buying by the foreign investors has uplifted the mood of the domestic investors", and that the market's near-term direction "appears to be north-bound", according to reports. He said profit-taking by domestic institutions and concerns about inflation could limit the rise.

## Oil and inflation

Brent crude, the international benchmark, traded at about $95 a barrel on Monday, roughly $1 below Friday's settlement, according to reports. The International Energy Agency has said, according to reports, that global oil supply is now running ahead of demand for the first time since the conflict involving Iran began, which has weighed on prices even as attacks on tankers continue around the Strait of Hormuz. India imports most of the crude it uses, so lower oil prices tend to support the rupee and ease pressure on inflation and the trade deficit.

Inflation remains a concern for investors. Government data released on Monday showed wholesale price inflation rising to 12.29% in October, up from 11.39% in September, with fuel and power prices nearly 33% higher than a year earlier.

## What happens next

Investors will watch the meeting of US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC summit in Shenzhen later this week for any easing of trade tensions. Oil prices, shipping in the Gulf and the flow of foreign money into Indian shares are the other things to watch.
